subject: physics
topic: Electrical energy and power, cost of electricity

kept.q: Which of the following best explains why electrical energy is sold to consumers in kilowatt-hours rather than in joules?
options: The kilowatt-hour is a smaller unit, so bills appear with smaller numbers for easy reading
The joule is too large a unit of energy to be measured by any meter
The kilowatt-hour is a more convenient practical unit since domestic energy use involves large numbers of joules
Electricity meters cannot be calibrated to read in joules at all
kept.explanation: A joule is a very small amount of energy, so household consumption would involve extremely large figures in joules. The kilowatt-hour is simply a more convenient practical unit for billing purposes.
kept.pidgin: Joule small too much, so house consumption go carry plenty big figures. Na im make kilowatt-hour good pass for billing.

kept.q: Two identical 60 W bulbs are connected in parallel across a 240 V supply. What is the total power delivered by the supply to both bulbs?
kept.explanation: In a parallel connection, each bulb draws its rated power independently from the supply. The total power is simply the sum of the two bulb ratings, 60 W + 60 W = 120 W.
kept.pidgin: For parallel connection, each bulb dey take im own power separate. Total power na just to add dem together, 60 W + 60 W = 120 W.

kept.q: A 240 V, 2 kW electric heater has its voltage reduced to 120 V while its resistance stays the same. What is the new power dissipated by the heater?
kept.explanation: Power is proportional to voltage squared when resistance is constant (P = V^2/R). Halving the voltage reduces power by a factor of 4, so the new power is 2000/4 = 500 W.
kept.pidgin: Power dey proportional to voltage squared when resistance no change (P = V^2/R). If you reduce voltage by half, power go reduce by four, wey give 2000/4 = 500 W.

kept.q: Adaeze's family runs a 1.5 kW refrigerator continuously for 24 hours daily and a 100 W reading lamp for 5 hours daily, for a 30-day month. If electricity costs N45 per kWh, what is the total monthly bill for both appliances?
kept.explanation: Fridge energy = 1.5 kW x 24 h x 30 days = 1080 kWh. Lamp energy = 0.1 kW x 5 h x 30 days = 15 kWh. Total = 1095 kWh, cost = 1095 x N45 = N49,275.
kept.pidgin: Fridge energy na 1080 kWh, lamp energy na 15 kWh, wey give total of 1095 kWh. If you multiply am by N45, you go get N49,275.

kept.q: An electric bulb is rated 220 V, 100 W. What is the resistance of the filament when the bulb is operating normally?
kept.explanation: Using R = V^2/P, resistance equals 220 squared divided by 100, which is 48400/100 = 484 ohms.
kept.pidgin: Make you use R = V^2/P, wey be 220 squared divide by 100. E go give you 48400/100, wey come be 484 ohms.

kept.q: A certain household electricity meter records that a family consumed 250 kWh of energy in a month. Which physical quantity does this reading directly represent?
options: The total charge that flowed through the appliances during the month
The total electrical energy converted by the appliances during the month
The average power consumed by the appliances at any instant
The peak instantaneous power drawn by the appliances
kept.explanation: A kilowatt-hour is a unit of energy, not power or charge. The meter reading therefore represents the total electrical energy that was converted into other forms by the appliances over the month.
kept.pidgin: Kilowatt-hour na unit for energy, no be power or charge. The meter reading show the total electrical energy wey appliances don use for the month.

kept.q: A generator supplies electrical power at a constant rate of 4000 W to a community. If the supply voltage is stepped down from 11000 V to 220 V by a transformer assumed to be 100% efficient, what is the current drawn in the low voltage secondary circuit?
kept.explanation: Since the transformer is ideal, power in equals power out, so current in secondary = Power/Voltage = 4000/220, which gives approximately 18.2 A.
kept.pidgin: Because transformer dey 100% efficient, power wey enter na im equal power wey go comot. Secondary current na Power divide by Voltage, wey be 4000/220 to give 18.2 A.

q.q: A 3 kW electric cooker is used for 4 hours every day for 2 weeks. If the Power Holding Company charges N50 per kWh, calculate the total cost of energy consumed.
q.explanation: Energy = 3 kW x 4 h x 14 days = 168 kWh. Cost = 168 x N50 = N8,400. Wait, check: 3x4=12, 12x14=168, 168x50=8400.
